title: SAP S/4HANA Sales Master Data Graph

summary.design_goal: Explain Sales behavior through the data, relationships, conditions, organizational context, and runtime events that mechanisms read.
summary.primary_question: Which maintained object supplied this value, under which scope and validity, and what does it change downstream?

behavior_layer.rule: Behavior profiles reference master-data nodes and process variants. They do not duplicate authoritative master-data entities.

six_questions: What is the object and who owns it?
At which organizational/key level is it valid?
Which fields are high leverage for Sales?
Which mechanism or process consumes it?
What is more specific and can refine/override the generic source?
Which failure signal proves I should inspect this object?
learning_model.memory_chain: PARTY → ADDRESS → PRODUCT → RELATIONSHIP → CONDITION → DECISION → DOCUMENT → EVENT

fast_paths.question: Wrong ship-to address or address-dependent defaults
Batch or serial trace is wrong
Recurring product set is not proposed

boundary_notes.rule: Maintained object with lifecycle beyond one sales document, for example BP or Product.
A learning and architecture layer that explains how master-data choices change runtime behavior. It is not another SAP master-data object.
Maintains a specific relationship such as customer-material or hierarchy membership.
Validity-based value selected by configured condition technique; the record is data, the access logic is configuration.
Determination procedures, condition types, access sequences, item categories and other control logic. Not master data.
Values copied or determined into inquiry/quotation/order/delivery/billing documents; after copy they have their own lifecycle.
Sales organization, distribution channel, division, plant and company code scope data/rules but are organizational structure, not classic business master data.

known_gaps: Sales deals/promotions and settlement-management data belong to a separate commercial-agreements layer rather than the universal Sales master-data core.
Dynamic product proposal and recommendation logic are optional/specialized order-entry layers beyond the core Sales Item Proposal.
Output parameter determination stays in the mechanism/configuration layer until its deployment-specific rule data model is modeled.
Product compliance/customer compliance is adjacent and should remain its own compliance graph.
Retail assortments/site/article master data remain industry-specific.
Empties/full-products behavior remains an industry extension until beverage or deposit logistics has its own model.

coverage_audit.conclusion: Core Sales master data coverage is broad. Remaining gaps are mainly specialized commercial-agreement, recommendation, compliance, and industry layers rather than missing universal Sales master objects.
core_covered: Business Partner multiple addresses and address usage
Customer sales-area data and partner functions
adjacent_covered: Units of measure and quantity constraints
intentional_boundaries: Sales organization, distribution channel, division, company code, plant, and shipping point are enterprise structure / organizational context, not classic business master data.

Pricing procedures, access sequences, condition types, partner procedures, item categories, schedule lines, copy control, output rules, and determination procedures are configuration/mechanisms, not master data records.
Tax classifications are customer/product attributes and tax results are condition/pricing outcomes; they do not require a second generic Sales master-data entity.
Payment terms, Incoterms, delivery priority, shipping condition, account-assignment groups, and similar values are high-leverage attributes of BP/product/sales views, not separate master objects.
Customer expected price is primarily transactional/inbound-order context and exception handling, not a universal reusable Sales master record.

Sales deals, promotions, condition contracts, settlement management, omnichannel promotion services, compliance, and Retail assortments are specialized commercial or industry layers and should stay outside the universal core.
